interface.title: Particle Picker Statistics Dashboard
interface.stage_of_work: Quality control of particle picking, after picking and before 2D classification and refinement
interface.what_it_is_for: Read a particle-coordinate file from a picking pipeline (RELION .star, CSV or EMAN2 .box) from the server, then show summary statistics, particle counts per micrograph, coordinate scatter and density plots, and defocus histograms so the scientist can judge picking quality.

data.note: Three sample files already on the server, typed in as paths: data/particles.star (48 particles, 5 micrographs, all charts drawn), data/particles.csv (20 particles, 5 micrographs; it has only CoordinateX, CoordinateY and MicrographName columns, so the defocus chart was empty as expected, and one row has a blank CoordinateX) and data/particles.box (20 particles, '0 micrographs'; every chart except the summary table was empty). The three files do not hold the same picking run. The page has no upload widget. The run downloaded a PNG from a chart's camera button (newplot.png), but kept no screen of it.

features.name: Server-path file loader with format selector and status banner
features.general: Type the path to a results file, say what format it is, load it, and get a coloured message giving the counts or the error, with the result panels shown or hidden to match
features.specific: Enter a path such as data/particles.star, pick the .star/.csv/.box radio button, press Load File, and read the green 'Successfully loaded N particles from M micrographs', the yellow 'Please enter a file path' or 'No particle data found', or the red 'File not found'. A wrong radio button can still 'succeed' with nonsense counts (65 particles, 0 micrographs)
steps: Type a file path relative to the server's working directory
Choose the format radio button (.star RELION, .csv Coordinates, .box EMAN2)
Press Load File
Read the alert banner; the result cards appear on success and are hidden on error
serves_tasks: Load a results file in its native format and check the counts it reports
Load results in the other supported formats and compare the counts each reports
See how the tool reports a bad input

features.name: Per-group count bar chart with name-on-hover
features.general: Bar chart of item counts per group, sorted from highest to lowest; hovering a bar shows the group's name, so the extremes can be spotted and identified
features.specific: 'Particle Distribution per Micrograph' bars indexed 0..4 by descending count, with the count printed on each bar; the tooltip shows the micrograph file name and particle count. Clicking a bar does not filter other charts
steps: Load a file
Scan the bar heights for very low or very high counts
Hover a bar to read the micrograph name and count
Optionally zoom, or save a PNG with the camera button
serves_tasks: Find images with unusually few or many detected items

features.name: Summary statistics table
features.general: A compact table of totals and spread for counts per group, which scrolls when there are more rows than fit
features.specific: Plotly table of Total Particles, Total Micrographs, and Avg/Min/Max/Std Particles Per Micrograph, scrolled with the mouse wheel
steps: Load a file
Read the first rows
Scroll inside the table to reveal Max and Std
serves_tasks: Load results in the other supported formats and compare the counts each reports

features.name: Coordinate scatter plus binned density heatmap
features.general: Show detected positions as points and as a binned count map side by side, with zoom and hover to inspect edges and hot spots
features.specific: 'Particle Coordinates (N points)' scatter of CoordinateX/Y (all micrographs pooled) with box-zoom and double-click reset, and a 'Particle Density Heatmap' (hot colour scale, Particle Count colourbar) whose tooltip gives x, y and z count. N in the title is the row count, not the number of points drawn
steps: Load a file that has coordinate columns
Hover points to read X/Y
Drag a box to zoom into a suspect region such as an edge
Double-click to reset
Hover heatmap cells to find the densest bin
serves_tasks: Look for edge artefacts or clustering among detected positions
Find the densest spots on a binned density map

features.name: Paired parameter histograms (DefocusU / DefocusV)
features.general: Two histograms side by side of two related per-item measurements, so outlying values stand out in both
features.specific: Defocus Distribution subplots for DefocusU and DefocusV; hovering gives the bin centre and count (for example 48.5k, 2), which shows an out-of-range CTF estimate
steps: Load a file that has DefocusU/DefocusV columns
Compare the shape of the two histograms
Hover an isolated bar to read its value and count
serves_tasks: Flag items whose measured parameter is far outside the main group

features.name: Histogram of counts per group
features.general: Histogram of how many groups have each item count, which shows at a glance whether a few groups fall far from the rest
features.specific: 'Distribution of Particles per Micrograph' histogram, with particles per micrograph on x and number of micrographs on y
steps: Load a file
Scroll to the Distribution Histogram
Read how many micrographs fall in each count bin
Compare isolated low or high bins with the summary table's Min and Max
serves_tasks: See how per-image counts are spread

screens_never_reached: A per-micrograph view of the scatter or heatmap: there is no micrograph selector, and clicking a bar in the distribution chart did not filter the other charts (screens/015.webp), so spatial plots always pool all micrographs

Defocus histograms for a CSV file: the sample data/particles.csv has only CoordinateX, CoordinateY and MicrographName, so the empty defocus panel (screens/018.webp) is the expected result, not a dashboard fault. No CSV with defocus columns was loaded

Any chart for a .box file: box_parser.py names the columns x/y/width/height, while statistics.py looks for 'MicrographName' and for 'coordinatex' or '_x'. Neither pattern matches, so for .box input every chart except the summary table is always empty (screens/020.webp). This is a limit of the tool, not of the sample file
not_done: Confirming consistent counts across formats could not be done: .star gave 48 particles from 5 micrographs, .csv gave 20 from 5, and .box gave 20 from 0. The sample files do not hold the same run.
The dashboard does not check that the chosen format matches the file. Reading the .star file as .csv reported 65 'particles' and 0 micrographs with no warning (screens/022.webp).
Clicking a bar in 'Particle Distribution per Micrograph' changed nothing else on the page (screens/015.webp).
Saving a chart as PNG: the camera button was clicked and newplot.png was downloaded, but no screen of the result was kept, so it is not recorded as a task.
I could not test files beyond the three samples. There is no upload, the paths are on the server, and the browser has no test files.
The box-select and lasso modebar tools were not tried in detail. No callback appeared to use chart selections, because clicking a bar changed nothing else on the page.
